sources.entry: HomeGallery - Browse personal photos and videos featuring tagging, mobile-friendly, and AI powered image discovery. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Nodejs/Docker

summary.one_liner: HomeGallery is a self-hosted web gallery for browsing personal photos and videos, with tagging, face and similar-image search, and a mobile-friendly PWA interface.
summary.what_it_does: The software indexes local media source directories (such as a Pictures folder or NAS share), generates previews and extracts metadata, then serves a browser-based gallery on localhost:3000 by default. It supports tagging with single and multi selection, an expressive query language with and/or/not operators, and endless scrolling through the archive. It offers reverse image lookup for finding similar photos, face detection and search by similar faces, and GEO location reverse lookups. Videos are transcoded, and media are identified by content so duplicates are processed once. It can also export a static web gallery, write XMP sidecar metadata, and stream to Chromecast devices.
use_cases: browsing personal photos and videos on a phone
finding similar photos without manual tagging
face search across a家庭 photo archive
tagging and searching a NAS media collection
exporting a static photo gallery website
how_to_run: Docker: mkdir -p data, then run docker run with -v for data and Pictures, -p 3000:3000 xemle/home-gallery
notable: Runs on low-power hardware such as Raspberry Pi and works with read-only or offline media sources after initial extraction
Media identified by content hash, so renames and moves do not require reprocessing previews
Optional self-hosted API for reverse image lookup and face recognition, though the default uses the public api.home-gallery.org
Claims a user with over 400,000 media files, though the whole database is loaded into the browser
caveats: Per the README, the project is a private spare-time project provided without warranty
Default AI features send preview images to the public api.home-gallery.org; local API setup requires technical knowledge and maintenance
The complete media database is loaded into the browser, so very large archives (about 100,000 media is cited as about 100 MB JSON) may be heavy
